summary: Phase 1 (User-Wise Pricing: Customer Accounts & Auth) fully tested. 19/19 pytest backend tests pass covering: registration (pending status, dup 409, invalid mobile), OTP request/verify (unregistered + registered + wrong OTP), password login (success/401/lockout-429 after 5 fails), full admin customer lifecycle (create, dup 409, approve, change-category, reset-password + verify new password logs in, suspend->403 for password AND otp, reactivate, reject, delete), pending customer login (returns status_label 'Pending Approval'), grandfathered active (existing 9876500011), pricing settings GET/PUT + persistence, toggle enforcement (enable_password_login=false -> 400, enable_otp=false -> 400) with proper restore to true. UI test verified: /register creates pending customer and shows correct success message; AuthDialog password login flow works (logout btn appears); AuthDialog OTP login flow shows dev_otp, verifies, logs in, pending banner visible on /account; admin login + /admin/customers status-tab-pending, search, approve action all functional; /admin/pricing-settings shows 9 toggles + behavior select + save. Zero critical bugs found.

issues: 'Customers' menu item appears twice (once under Customer Support and once under Catalog & Sales) - minor duplication, could confuse admin users
React a11y console warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby for DialogContent'. Add DialogDescription for screen readers.

action_items: (Optional) Add DialogDescription to AuthDialog to silence a11y warning
(Optional) De-duplicate 'Customers' entry in admin sidebar navigation
critical_code_review_comments: auth_routes.register: 'existing = find_one({mobile: {$regex: mobile + "$"}})' fallback used before normalized_mobile is guaranteed for old records — this is intentional for migration but the same $regex is unanchored at start, so a stored mobile '19876500011' would match '9876500011'. In practice normalize_mobile trims to 10 digits so risk is low; still consider anchoring with ^ once migration is complete.

auth_routes.otp/verify: expiry check happens AFTER marking wrong_attempts and AFTER matching OTP — correct order, but note if user submits correct OTP after expiry they'll get 400 'expired' which is fine.

admin_routes.update_customer: does not re-check duplicate mobile — an admin could set customer B's mobile to customer A's mobile creating a duplicate. Consider adding a duplicate guard on PUT if mobile changed.
pricing.update_settings: no field whitelist — any arbitrary key from body is persisted into settings doc. Consider whitelisting to prevent injection of unrelated keys.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 1 is stable. Phases 2-4 (customer/category-specific pricing, price protection, last-confirmed-order pricing) are NOT built yet — do not test them. Pricing settings toggles for those categories exist but only wire up in later phases. Restored enable_otp=true and enable_password_login=true after enforcement tests.
